result.summary: Six map chips were checked against live sources and our own store: Hail, Heat, Wind, Flood, Fire and Air. Ready now from our own store: Hail (MRMS radar estimate of hail 1 inch or more; 144,522 of 450,765 Montana cells had at least one such day in five years; one palette PNG of about 42 KB covers Montana at native cell size and can be placed like the radar frames), Heat (NOAA nClimGrid-Daily grid estimate of days at or above 90 F; the Billings cell matches the airport record within 2 days for July 2021 to June 2022) and Wind (NWS high wind and wind advisory products by public forecast zone; 83 public zones in the current edition; station gusts are airport points, 1,261 station days at 50 knots or more). Flood: the store holds 43 flood warning, 37 areal flood warning, 35 flood watch, 10 flood advisory and 548 areal flood advisory rows, and 277 Montana river gauges have live NWS flood categories, but FEMA flood zones are left out by repo decision D38 (a hazard and insurance designation) and the FEMA terms could not be read here; the FEMA layer has 31,335 polygons in the Montana box. Fire: the NIFC current perimeter service (5 perimeters in the box, newest updated 2026-10-21) and historic service (6,879 in the box) are live; the USGS MTBS national perimeter zip (390 MB) says there are no restrictions on use beyond acknowledgement; the 2023 USFS wildfire hazard potential raster (351 MB zip) says it can be used without additional permissions or fees. Air: the EPA AirNow API returns 401 without a key, so it needs an account; NOAA Hazard Mapping System smoke polygons are live (116 polygons for 2026-10-24) but their public domain status is not verified; PurpleAir terms could not be read. Every legend must say the source, the estimate type and the data age; no chip may say no risk; missing data shows as data unavailable. Notes: notes.md was not written because the agent rules forbid report .md files; the commands, quotes and sizes are in /home/user/hail-b5/out/ref/risk-sources/evidence.txt (plain text), and the sample downloads were deleted after measuring (the label folder is 2.2 MB, holding small saved pages and the scripts).
blockers: FEMA NFHL terms not read: the FEMA disclaimer page returned 403 (a content delivery network block page) to curl and 404 to the fetch tool; the flood-zone page returned 403; the Map Service Center home is a shell. The repo's own record says the flood-zone wording needs counsel first (DECISIONS.md line 941, counsel item 12). Do not build a FEMA layer until the owner and counsel decide.

PurpleAir terms and API documentation not readable: the terms page gave only a heading to the fetch tool and a 77-character shell to curl; the API pages are client-side shells. Licence, key rules and commercial use are unverified, so PurpleAir must not be used until its terms are read.
AirNow data terms and price not verified: the request without a key returns 401; the About page has no reuse text; the docs page does not state a price.
NOAA Hazard Mapping System public domain status not verified: the OSPO page has no reuse statement, the NOAA disclaimer page has no public domain text, and the NWS disclaimer covers NWS pages only.

USGS flood inundation maps not read: the USGS flood inundation page and the USGS copyright page returned 403 (block pages). Only one Montana gauge (CFMM8, Flathead River at Columbia Falls) has NWS inundation mapping enabled, out of 277 Montana gauges checked.

Wildfire hazard potential: the reuse sentence is verified ('can be used without additional permissions or fees') but the words 'public domain' do not appear; the Montana portion was not extracted from the 351 MB national zip, and the raster format inside the zip was not listed. The Wildfire Risk to Communities methods page does not name the raster, so the link from that site to the raster is unverified.

MTBS: Montana portion and burn severity rasters not measured (only the national perimeter zip, 389,925,218 bytes, was sized and read). The direct-download site moved to the Burn Severity site and the mtbs.gov page announces an outage starting 2026-10-28 at 8:00 PM for maintenance.

Sizes marked as rough are extrapolations from 200-feature samples (FEMA flood zones about 1.3 GB and NIFC historic perimeters about 104 MB as GeoJSON at full geometry); the full layers were not downloaded.

Storage: D38 (wt-b5 DECISIONS.md, the budget paragraph near line 815) records that all of hail/ breaks its caps (162.0 MB against 60 MB; j/ with j/e 86.2 MB against 40 MB) and that the owner or supervisor rules on both.
